AntmazeGiantNavigate.docstring: OGBench antmaze-giant-navigate. State is qpos (15 floats); the dataset suffix selects a task and does not reach the renderer, so it shares a baked plate with the other antmaze-giant cells.
AntmazeGiantNavigate.parity_note: AGENT-PIXEL PARITY (supersample 2, against MuJoCo at its default offsamples=4, 25 cells x 64 states). Every disagreement is inside the agent's own silhouette: the baked plate is exact by construction, non-agent pixels are 99.88-99.99% bit-identical, and that residual is the reference's multisampling bleeding agent colour into neighbouring wall/floor pixels. On agent-interior pixels (eroded by one, so coverage is not in play) the shader reaches 48-84% within 1/255 for pointmaze (mean 1.2-2.5/255), 0-51% for antmaze and 0-3% for humanoidmaze. The legged numbers are not a shading result: at the official whole-maze camera the ant is 12-70 px and the humanoid 4-21 px of 50176, and eroding leaves as few as 1 interior pixel, so their agreement is a statement about a silhouette under the reference's coverage rule. Against a NON-multisampled reference the same shader reaches 92.4% within 1/255 over 13,069 pooled agent-interior pixels (mean 0.88/255), which localises most of the remaining gap in MSAA sample positions -- GPU-specific, not recoverable by fitting -- rather than in shading. Three mechanisms were tried and are recorded so they are not retried: the fixed-function composition (FIXED - specular is additive and white and the texture modulates the whole primary colour, which took wall tops from 13/255 worst to 2/255 and made vertical wall faces bit-exact); Gouraud interpolation over MuJoCo's sphere/capsule tessellation (REFUTED - ten (slices, stacks, phase, diagonal) variants all scored 0.0-0.2% exact against 1.6% for plain per-pixel, which is also what sub-pixel triangles predict); and a mis-shaped specular lobe (REFUTED - a 24-knot piecewise-linear lobe fitted under four light/specular geometries, headlight directional or point crossed with Blinn or Phong, could not explain floor and agent with one curve).

OGBCube.docstring:
OGBench manipulation Cube (swm/OGBCube-v0), fidelity_tier='visual'.

The frame is a MuJoCo-baked static plate composited with mujoco_warp's batch ray-caster for the movers, at swm's registered 224 px from the model camera 'front_pixels'. State is (qpos, mocap_pos), 24 dimensions. qvel is excluded because it reaches no pixel and mocap_quat because it is the identity everywhere in the registered distribution.

THIS IS A VISUAL TIER CELL, NOT A PARITY ONE. Three lighting terms in mujoco_warp disagree with MuJoCo and are declared in visual_fidelity and visual_note rather than chased: the global directional light, the spot's distance attenuation, and the headlight on mover pixels. A fourth, the out-of-range spot cutoff, WAS fixed and now lives in the shared render/mjwarp.py path. The translucent goal marker is a fifth, separate residual: mujoco_warp has no alpha path.

There is NO CPU backend: device='cpu' raises rather than silently using the GPU (CPU3D-OGB-1).

visual_fidelity.measured_at: mujoco 3.12.0 / ogbench 1.2.1 reference; 224 px, camera front_pixels, 8 independent draws of 64 states from the env's own pool (reset + 0-25 random actions) on an RTX 3090 under MUJOCO_GL=egl, against swm's own render(); the declared value is the WORST of the eight and draw_spread carries the range, for mean_abs/within8_frac/ssim AND for interior_exact_frac, all_exact_frac and interior_frac. MEASURED THROUGH THE CHECK THAT GRADES IT, `check_visual_fidelity`, and one of the eight draws IS the draw the check takes -- it calls `sample_states(n)` with no rng, which is seed 0, the same fixed draw every time. The previous declaration was measured by a probe that averaged |diff| over the colour channels while `pixel_agreement` averages the per-pixel channel MAX, so it read 0.89/255 low and no widening rule could have covered the gap. The frame is a baked MuJoCo plate composited with MJWarp movers through the mover segmentation LUT, with gl_rounding and the shared out-of-range-spot correction applied. job 6433493 on gpu2109.oscar.ccv.brown.edu

OGBCube.visual_note: THREE declared residuals, all attributed by measurement before this class was written, and all structural to mujoco_warp rather than to this scene. (1) THE `global` DIRECTIONAL LIGHT is the largest remaining term: neutralising it on both sides moves interior exactness 0.347 -> 0.702. It is the castshadow light, and turning shadows OFF makes agreement worse, so the disagreement is in the light and not in its shadow. (2) THE SPOT'S DISTANCE ATTENUATION: after the shared out-of-range-cutoff correction, removing the spot entirely still adds +0.113, because MJWarp takes attenuation = 1/(1,d,d^2).(1,0,0) = 1 and MuJoCo evidently does something else with the same light_attenuation. (3) THE HEADLIGHT IS A MOVER-PIXEL TERM: interior barely moves (+0.001) while mover exactness goes 0.757 -> 0.896, which is what a light along the camera axis does. A fourth thing is NOT a residual and was checked: ambient. Zeroing it makes agreement WORSE, so MJWarp already agrees with MuJoCo about it. ALSO DECLARED, AND SEPARATE FROM THE SHADING: the translucent goal marker `target_object_0` renders at alpha 0.2 and mujoco_warp's shader reads only color[0..2], so it has no alpha path and would paint the marker opaque. Measured share of the frame: 0.61% (Cube) / 0.15% (Scene), against the 1.2-1.5% Fetch already declares for the same mechanism. WHERE THE RESIDUAL IS NOT: the floor. It is the baked plate, composited in wherever the mover LUT says MJWarp did not hit a mover, and the measured result is interior-exact 0.958 (Cube) / 0.922 (Scene) and whole-frame 0.872 / 0.775 over three independent 64-state draws. An earlier version of this cell masked with `seg >= 0` -- true wherever MJWarp hit ANYTHING, floor included -- so the plate reached only the sky and the same scene scored 0.351 interior-exact. That composite bug was worth more than every lighting term above combined.

OGBCube.docstring:
OGBench manipulation Cube (swm/OGBCube-v0), fidelity_tier='visual'.

The frame is a MuJoCo-baked static plate composited with mujoco_warp's batch ray-caster for the movers, at swm's registered 224 px from the model camera 'front_pixels'. State is (qpos, mocap_pos), 24 dimensions. qvel is excluded because it reaches no pixel and mocap_quat because it is the identity everywhere in the registered distribution.

THIS IS A VISUAL TIER CELL, NOT A PARITY ONE. Three lighting terms in mujoco_warp disagree with MuJoCo and are declared in visual_fidelity and visual_note rather than chased: the global directional light, the spot's distance attenuation, and the headlight on mover pixels. A fourth, the out-of-range spot cutoff, WAS fixed and now lives in the shared render/mjwarp.py path. The translucent goal marker is a fifth, separate residual: mujoco_warp has no alpha path.

There is NO CPU backend: device='cpu' raises rather than silently using the GPU (CPU3D-OGB-1).

visual_fidelity.measured_at: mujoco 3.12.0 / ogbench 1.2.1 reference; 224 px, camera front_pixels, 8 independent draws of 64 states from the env's own pool (reset + 0-25 random actions) on an RTX 3090 under MUJOCO_GL=egl, against swm's own render(); the declared value is the WORST of the eight and draw_spread carries the range, for mean_abs/within8_frac/ssim AND for interior_exact_frac, all_exact_frac and interior_frac. MEASURED THROUGH THE CHECK THAT GRADES IT, `check_visual_fidelity`, and one of the eight draws IS the draw the check takes -- it calls `sample_states(n)` with no rng, which is seed 0, the same fixed draw every time. The previous declaration was measured by a probe that averaged |diff| over the colour channels while `pixel_agreement` averages the per-pixel channel MAX, so it read 0.89/255 low and no widening rule could have covered the gap. The frame is a baked MuJoCo plate composited with MJWarp movers through the mover segmentation LUT, with gl_rounding and the shared out-of-range-spot correction applied. job 6433493 on gpu2109.oscar.ccv.brown.edu

OGBCube.visual_note: THREE declared residuals, all attributed by measurement before this class was written, and all structural to mujoco_warp rather than to this scene. (1) THE `global` DIRECTIONAL LIGHT is the largest remaining term: neutralising it on both sides moves interior exactness 0.347 -> 0.702. It is the castshadow light, and turning shadows OFF makes agreement worse, so the disagreement is in the light and not in its shadow. (2) THE SPOT'S DISTANCE ATTENUATION: after the shared out-of-range-cutoff correction, removing the spot entirely still adds +0.113, because MJWarp takes attenuation = 1/(1,d,d^2).(1,0,0) = 1 and MuJoCo evidently does something else with the same light_attenuation. (3) THE HEADLIGHT IS A MOVER-PIXEL TERM: interior barely moves (+0.001) while mover exactness goes 0.757 -> 0.896, which is what a light along the camera axis does. A fourth thing is NOT a residual and was checked: ambient. Zeroing it makes agreement WORSE, so MJWarp already agrees with MuJoCo about it. ALSO DECLARED, AND SEPARATE FROM THE SHADING: the translucent goal marker `target_object_0` renders at alpha 0.2 and mujoco_warp's shader reads only color[0..2], so it has no alpha path and would paint the marker opaque. Measured share of the frame: 0.61% (Cube) / 0.15% (Scene), against the 1.2-1.5% Fetch already declares for the same mechanism. WHERE THE RESIDUAL IS NOT: the floor. It is the baked plate, composited in wherever the mover LUT says MJWarp did not hit a mover, and the measured result is interior-exact 0.958 (Cube) / 0.922 (Scene) and whole-frame 0.872 / 0.775 over three independent 64-state draws. An earlier version of this cell masked with `seg >= 0` -- true wherever MJWarp hit ANYTHING, floor included -- so the plate reached only the sky and the same scene scored 0.351 interior-exact. That composite bug was worth more than every lighting term above combined.
